chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, who said:

I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) being asked about the prayer in the ship, so he said: 'If you are able to go out to the hard ground, then go out. But if you are not able, so pray standing. But if you are not able, so pray seated, and investigate (the direction of) the Qiblah'.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for praying in a ship if one cannot stand?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes a pragmatic hierarchy for shipboard prayer, prioritizing standing but permitting sitting when space or stability is limited, reflecting the Shia principle of ease in travel. This ruling underscores the flexibility of Islamic jurisprudence in adapting ritual obligations to physical constraints, ensuring the continuity of worship without undue hardship. The emphasis on facing the Qiblah as much as possible highlights the balance between strict adherence to direction and the practical realities of maritime travel.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad Bin Isa who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullahasws being asked about the Salāt performed in the ship, so heasws was saying: ‘If you are able to go out to the hard ground, then go out. But if you are not able, so pray Salāt standing. But if you are not able, so pray Salāt seated, and investigate (the direction of) the Qiblah’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Hammad ibn ‘Isa who has said the following: “

I once heard abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, being asked about Salah (prayer) in the ship. He (the Imam) said, ‘If you can come out to hard ground, you must do so; but if you cannot do so, then perform Salah (prayer) standing, if you cannot do so, then perform Salah (prayer) while sitting and try to make it toward al-Qiblah (al-Ka‘bah).’”
